_comment: The five pilot trace sources. Three judge families (openai, anthropic, google)
and two non-judge controls (deepseek, meta), which is the two-axis design the
suggested-actions document asks for: capability and judge-family.
route: which base_url + key to use. All three go through the `openai` SDK -
OpenAI natively, Google via its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and OpenRouter for
Anthropic and the open-weight models. One client class, three endpoints, three
keys, exactly as the keys in .env are scoped.
anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.7 does not exist on OpenRouter (the Sonnet line is
4, 4.5, 4.6, 5). claude-opus-4.7 is used because it is the judge the published
framework runs, so E0 stays the published baseline.
price_per_m is a SNAPSHOT taken from the OpenRouter catalogue on 2026-09-17,
used only to estimate and report spend. It is not authoritative: run
`python -m evaluator_pilot_17092026.run_traces --check` to re-read live prices.
max_tokens is a per-model ceiling. The three reasoning models get 8192 because
their thinking is billed inside the completion budget: at 4096 a long derivation
returns finish_reason=length with empty content, which run_traces records as a
failure rather than as a trace. Llama is capped at 2048 because it does not
reason and its archive completions sit near 400 tokens.
GPT-5 goes through OpenRouter, not the OpenAI key. OPENAI_API_KEY in .env
returns 401 (checked 2026-09-17), the same state ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was in.
openai/gpt-5 on OpenRouter is $1.25 in / $10.00 out, identical to the direct
API, so nothing about the estimate changes. The direct route is kept in
fallback: swap it back when a working key exists and --check will confirm it.
Ceilings raised after the first pass, from what it measured. At 8192, GPT-5
ran out of budget mid-reasoning on 5 of 60 items and DeepSeek R1 on 28 of 60;
R1 also returned three all-reasoning responses of about 6,500 tokens. Claude,
Gemini and Llama finished 60 of 60 and keep their ceilings. The ceiling is an
upper bound, not a reservation: a short answer still bills short.
DeepSeek is r1-0528, not r1. Plain deepseek/deepseek-r1 has one provider whose
output cap is 16,000 tokens, and R1 writes 30,000+ characters of reasoning on the
iterative items, so it truncated before writing an answer on 28 of 60. All four
r1-0528 providers cap at 32,000 or above, so max_tokens 32768 is honoured whichever
one routing picks. SiliconFlow offers 147,456 if that ever needs pinning.
Gemini and GPT-5 raised to 32768 after verify_traces found 19 rows ending at
finish_reason=length. Provider maxima are 65,536 and 128,000, so the ceiling was
ours. Gemini needs the room for a reason worth knowing: its OpenAI-compatible
endpoint does not report thinking tokens in usage (reasoning_tokens is None on
every row), so thinking was consuming the budget invisibly and the visible answer
was cut at 323-1,455 tokens. That also means the cost this runner computes for
Gemini is a FLOOR, not the bill - it is the only model with that gap.

superseded.reason: single provider (Novita), hard 16,000-token output cap; 28 of 60 items truncated mid-reasoning
